title: Moringa Chutney Powder (Drumstick Leaf Podi)
description: A aromatic, spiced chutney powder made with dried moringa leaves, roasted lentils, and garlic. A nutrient-rich condiment perfect with rice, dosa, and idli.

subSteps: Pick fresh moringa leaves from the stems, discarding any yellowed or damaged leaves
Rinse the moringa leaves thoroughly under running water and pat dry with a clean cloth
Spread the moringa leaves on a microwave-safe plate in a single layer
Microwave on high heat for 3-4 minutes in 1-minute intervals, stirring between each interval
The leaves should be completely dried and crispy, breaking apart easily when touched
Remove from microwave and let cool completely (approximately 5 minutes)
You should have approximately 2 cups of loosely packed dried moringa leaves
VALIDATION: Leaves should be completely dry and crispy, not wilted or soft. They should break apart easily when crushed between fingers. No moisture should remain.
Measure 2 tbsp chana dal (Bengal gram)
Measure 2 tbsp urad dal (split black gram)
Measure 10-12 dry red chillies (Guntur chillies preferred for best flavor)
Measure 1.5 tsp coriander seeds (dhaniyalu)
Measure 1.5 tsp cumin seeds (jeelakara)
Peel 8-10 garlic cloves and set aside
Take a small lemon-sized ball of tamarind (approximately 1 tbsp)
Clean the tamarind by removing any seeds or stringy bits
Measure 1/4 tsp asafoetida (hing)
Measure 1 tsp peanut or sesame oil
VALIDATION: All ingredients measured and prepared. Tamarind should be cleaned of seeds and stringy bits. Garlic cloves should be peeled.

ingredients.name: Dry red chillies
ingredients.notes: Guntur chillies work best, adjust for heat preference

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves
ingredients.notes: peeled, added raw at the end

subSteps: Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat
Add 0.5 tsp peanut or sesame oil to the pan
Once oil is hot, add 2 tbsp chana dal (Bengal gram) to the pan
Add 2 tbsp urad dal (split black gram) to the pan
Roast continuously, stirring frequently with a spoon, for 2-3 minutes
Watch the color carefully - the dals should turn from pale to light golden brown
The dals should release a rich, nutty aroma when properly roasted
Do not allow the dals to burn - they should remain light golden, not dark brown
VALIDATION: Both dals should be light golden brown with a strong nutty aroma. Some pieces may stick to the pan slightly. The roasted dals should smell warm and toasted.
Lower the flame to low-medium
Add 1.5 tsp coriander seeds to the pan
Add 10-12 dry red chillies to the pan
Stir-fry the mixture continuously for approximately 2 minutes
Watch the chillies carefully - they should swell slightly and change color
The mixture should become fragrant with warm spice aromas
Do not let the chillies burn - they should darken slightly but not turn black
VALIDATION: Chillies should swell and change to a darker red-brown color. The kitchen should smell strongly of roasted chillies and coriander. Spices should be fragrant but not burnt.
Add 1.5 tsp cumin seeds to the pan
Add tamarind pieces (approximately 1 lemon-sized ball) to the pan
Add 1/4 tsp asafoetida (hing) to the pan
Stir well to combine all ingredients
Sauté for just 1 minute to warm up the tamarind and awaken the cumin oils
The mixture should be warm and fragrant
Turn off the heat immediately after 1 minute
VALIDATION: All ingredients should be warm and aromatic. Tamarind should soften slightly from the heat. Cumin oils should be released, creating a warm, spiced aroma.
While the pan is still warm (after turning off heat), toss the 2 cups of crisp, dried moringa leaves directly into the warm pan
Stir gently to combine the leaves with the warm spice mixture
The residual heat from the pan will draw out any remaining microscopic moisture from the leaves
Spread the mixture on a clean plate to cool completely
Allow the mixture to cool for approximately 10 minutes at room temperature
The leaves should remain crispy and not become soft or wilted
Once cooled, you should have a fragrant, dry mixture of moringa leaves and toasted spices
VALIDATION: Moringa leaves should remain crispy and dry. The mixture should be cool to the touch. The aroma should be complex - nutty, spicy, tangy, and herbaceous all at once.
Add the cooled spice-and-moringa mixture to a dry mixer jar
Add 0.5 tsp salt to the mixer jar
Do not add liquid - the mixer should work with completely dry ingredients
Close the mixer lid securely
Pulse the mixer 4-5 times, each pulse lasting about 2-3 seconds
Do not blend continuously - use short pulses to maintain texture
After each pulse, check the consistency - you want a semi-coarse powder, not a fine flour
The mixture should have visible texture with specks of moringa, chillies, and spices visible
Do not over-grind - the goal is a grainy podi, not a paste

VALIDATION: The podi should resemble coarse breadcrumbs with visible green specks from moringa leaves and red specks from chillies. It should not be a fine powder. You should see individual ingredients clearly.
Add 8-10 peeled garlic cloves to the mixer jar containing the semi-coarse podi
Pulse the mixer 2-3 times, each pulse lasting 2-3 seconds
The dampness of the garlic will help the podi bind together beautifully without turning it into a paste
Stop pulsing when the garlic is roughly broken up and distributed throughout
Do not over-blend - the garlic should be in small pieces, not minced fine
Transfer the finished podi to a clean, dry glass jar
Let it cool completely before sealing the jar

VALIDATION: The garlic should be roughly broken up and distributed throughout the podi. The mixture should hold together slightly when squeezed but still have a crumbly texture. It should not be wet or paste-like. The aroma should be pungent with fresh garlic, warm spices, and fresh moringa.
